what_its_for: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla) is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of breast cancer called HER2-positive breast cancer. It is used in adults whose cancer has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic) or has come back after earlier treatment. It combines two medicines in one: trastuzumab, which targets the HER2 protein on cancer cells, and emtansine, which kills those cancer cells directly.
how_to_take: This medicine is given by a nurse or doctor as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or IV line. You will receive it at a hospital, cancer center, or infusion clinic. You do NOT take this medicine at home as a pill or injection. Your first infusion usually takes about 90 minutes. If you tolerate it well, future infusions may take about 30 minutes. You will be watched closely during and after each infusion for any reactions.
dosing: The usual dose is 3.6 mg per kilogram (mg/kg) of your body weight, given once every 3 weeks (21-day cycle). Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your weight. Your doctor may lower your dose or pause treatment if you experience certain side effects. Never try to adjust your own dose. Your treatment schedule and number of cycles will be decided by your cancer care team.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital, you will not be giving it to yourself at home. If you miss or need to reschedule an appointment, call your doctor or treatment center as soon as possible to set up a new time. Try not to delay your treatment for more than a few days without talking to your doctor first.
storage: This medicine is stored and prepared by pharmacy and healthcare professionals. You do not need to store it at home. For your information: the unopened vials are stored in a refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and are kept out of direct light. Once mixed and ready for infusion, the solution should be used within 4 hours at room temperature or within 24 hours if kept refrigerated.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant while receiving this medicine, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 7 months after your last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 7 months after your last dose. Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), and other NSAIDs, or blood thinners unless your doctor approves, as this medicine can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid activities that could cause injury or bleeding if your platelet counts are low. Tell all of your doctors and dentists that you are receiving this medicine before any procedures.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding, including blood in your urine, stool, or vomit; severe stomach or abdominal pain; yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; shortness of breath, chest pain, or a fast or irregular heartbeat; severe headache, confusion, vision changes, or seizures; numbness, tingling, or pain in your hands or feet; swelling of your legs or ankles; pain or burning at the infusion site; or any allergic reaction symptoms such as rash, hives, dizziness, or trouble breathing during or after your infusion.
when_it_works: It is hard to know exactly when this medicine will start working because everyone is different. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular scans, blood tests, and physical exams. Some patients may see improvements within the first few cycles, while for others it may take longer. Continue going to all of your scheduled appointments even if you do not feel different right away. Do not stop treatment without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 4 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for 7 months after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor will check your liver function before and during treatment. If you have liver problems, your dose may need to be adjusted or treatment may need to be stopped. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years old. Older adults (65 and older): Older adults may be more likely to experience certain side effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely.
